explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/431 (Ostmann's 'inverse Goldbach problem'): are there two infinite sets A and B such that A + B agrees with the primes up to finitely many exceptions? The variant states Ostmann's conjecture in its usual stronger form: for all A, B ⊆ ℕ each with at least two elements (Set.Nontrivial), the symmetric difference (A + B) ∆ {primes} is infinite. This is the standard formulation of the inverse Goldbach conjecture (compare the page's mention of Elsholtz's three-set result for sets 'of size at least 2') and is correctly formalised; it implies the negative answer to the page's question. The documentation concern is the status: the declaration is tagged 'research solved' citing a 2026 OpenAI preprint, whereas the erdosproblems.com page as fetched today still says only 'The answer is surely no' and lists partial results, so I could not confirm the claimed resolution from the cited page.
